verdictUnknown: No problems found; some items could not be read
modelNotInTable: The model identifier is not in the built-in table; the name is the device's own
unitRetailDetail: M: a unit sold at retail
unitRefurbishedDetail: F: a unit Apple refurbished (Certified Refurbished)
unitReplacementDetail: N: a whole unit Apple handed out as a service replacement
unitEngravedDetail: P: a retail unit engraved to order on Apple's website
unitDemoDetail: 3: a demo unit from a store's display
unitOtherDetail: The model number starts with “{prefix}”, not a usual retail prefix
regionNotInTable: The region code is not in the built-in table
regionChinaBrickMismatch: RegionInfo={region} but ChinaBrick={chinaBrick}: the region may have been rewritten
productionChipNoDetail: ProductionSOC = false: the chip is dev-fused, as on engineering units
betaBuildDetail: The build number ends in a lowercase letter: a beta release
releaseInternalDetail: ReleaseType = {type}: an Apple internal build, as on engineering units
serialLegacy12Bad: A 12-character serial that does not decode by Apple's scheme; check it on Apple's website
serialRandom: Randomized serial (2021 on), without a date of manufacture
serialOddLength: A serial of {length, number, ::group-off} characters is not a usual Apple format
serialWeekAmbiguous: week {week, number, ::group-off} of {year, number, ::group-off} (the year may be off by a decade)
sourcesDisagree: The sources disagree: a value may have been rewritten
imeiMissing: The device has cellular but reports no IMEI; its baseband may be faulty
imeiLength: An IMEI has 15 digits, this one {length, number, ::group-off}
imeiLuhnFailed: The IMEI's check digit is wrong (Luhn check failed)
activationUnactivatedDetail: Not activated yet (new, or just erased)
activationFactoryDetail: FactoryActivated: a factory or test activation, not a user's
findMyOnDetail: Before the sale the seller must sign out of their Apple Account and turn off Find My, or the phone cannot be activated after an erase
findMyUnknown: The device does not report it; check in Settings > [your name] > Find My
supervisedDetail: The device is supervised, as company and school devices are
profilesUnread: The configuration profiles could not be read
mdmEnrolledDetail: An organization enrolled the device through Apple Business Manager: after an erase, activation forces it into their management
mdmProfileDetail: An MDM profile, or one the user may not remove, is installed: the device is managed remotely, and its manager can see or restrict it
jailbreakAFC2: The afc2 service is present (only a jailbreak registers it)
jailbreakNone: No jailbreak apps and no afc2 service (a jailbreak that leaves no trace cannot be ruled out)
jailbreakUnread: Could not read the app list or check the afc2 service
jailbreakNoApps: No afc2 service, but the app list could not be read to look for jailbreak apps
jailbreakNoAFC2: No jailbreak apps in the app list, but the afc2 service could not be checked
developerModeDetail: Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode is on
brickStateDetail: BrickState = true: the device is locked and not activated
bootArgsDetail: boot-args are set in NVRAM, which are empty on retail units: the device may have been jailbroken, downgraded or debugged
basebandNotReady: BasebandStatus = {status}: the baseband's information is not fully ready
basebandMissing: A cellular device that reports no baseband version: its baseband may be faulty or missing, or the logic board was repaired
healthFromCapacity: Computed from the full charge capacity of {max, number, ::group-off} mAh and the design capacity of {design, number, ::group-off} mAh; may differ slightly from Settings
healthComputed: computed from the capacity, about {percent, number, ::.0}% ({max, number, ::group-off} / {design, number, ::group-off} mAh)
healthFromGauge: The maximum capacity the battery's gas gauge reports
healthFromLog: The maximum capacity in the system's analytics log, as Settings > Battery Health shows it (logged {date})
healthLogOld: That record is {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} old and may not be current
capacityNotRead: The battery's capacity was not read
healthAboveDesignDetail: The full charge capacity is well above the design capacity, which a genuine battery never reaches; common with high-capacity aftermarket batteries, so this figure is not the real health
healthNear80: Close to the 80% mark for a replacement
healthBelow80: Below 80%: replacing the battery is advised
batteryCyclesDisagree: The IORegistry counts {ioreg, number, ::group-off} cycles, the diagnostics' gas gauge {gauge, number, ::group-off}: the sources disagree
cyclesFromLog: Not read from the gas gauge; from the system's analytics log ({date})
batteryOverCapacity: The full charge capacity of {max, number, ::group-off} mAh is {percent, number, ::group-off}% of the design capacity of {design, number, ::group-off} mAh (genuine batteries measured at most about 105%)
batteryLogCyclesHigher: The analytics log of {date} counted {logged, number, ::group-off} cycles, the battery now has {now, number, ::group-off}: it was replaced since
batteryTooFewCycles: The phone was made about {years, number, ::.0} years ago, yet its battery has {cycles, number, ::group-off} cycles: it was likely replaced
batteryOriginUnread: The battery's capacity and cycle count were not read
batteryNoSignsDetail: No sign of a raised capacity, or of cycles at odds with the phone's age; whether it is genuine, Settings > Battery and Parts and Service History tell
noAnalytics: The device holds no analytics logs (Settings > Privacy & Security > Analytics & Improvements > Share iPhone Analytics is off, or the device was erased or restored lately; logs appear about a day after it is turned on)
noBatteryInAnalytics: The analytics logs hold no battery records
faceIDFDRFailedDetail: FDRValidated = false: the Face ID module does not match the factory pairing data and may have been replaced or repaired (read from the field's meaning; no sample confirms it yet)
faceIDFDRPassed: FDRValidated = true (matches the factory pairing data)
faceIDFailedDetail: {key} = {code, number, ::group-off} (0 on a working unit). Face ID's hardware self test failed, as when Face ID is broken or a screen replacement damaged its dot projector or flood illuminator; enroll a face to test it
faceIDUnread: This model has Face ID, but its self test could not be read; enroll a face to test it
touchIDCalibrationFDR: Calibration from the factory pairing data (MesaCalBlobSource = FDR)
touchIDSelfTestFailedDetail: MesaSelfTest = {result} (OK on a working unit; no failing sample yet). Common when the Home button or its cable is damaged or was replaced; enroll a fingerprint to test it
touchIDOnlineDetail: The sensor is connected and reports its serial number, and its calibration comes from the factory pairing data (MesaCalBlobSource = FDR), as on units whose self test passed; this iOS version gives no self test result, so enroll a fingerprint to test it
touchIDNoSerial: The sensor reports no serial number
touchIDCalibrationOther: Its calibration does not come from the factory pairing data ({source})
touchIDUnsure: Its state cannot be confirmed; enroll a fingerprint to test it
touchIDMissingDetail: This model has Touch ID, but the system finds no fingerprint sensor: common when the Home button or its cable is damaged, disconnected or replaced
partsUnread: The parts could not be read; enroll a fingerprint to test it
setupUnfinishedDetail: The device is still in activation or the Setup Assistant
manualPartsHistory: Settings > General > About > Parts and Service History: iOS's own verdict on whether the display, battery, {bio} and cameras are genuine, which this tool cannot read over the cable; be sure to look at it (iOS 15.2 and later, some models)
manualBatteryHealth: Settings > Battery > Battery Health: compare it with this report; “Service” there means the battery has aged even when its maximum capacity is above 80% (iOS says so when its resistance is high)
manualTrueTone: Was the display replaced? Long-press the brightness slider in Control Center: iPhone 8 / X and later have a True Tone switch; without it the display was likely replaced (not readable over the cable)
manualCoverage: Check the model, color, warranty and activation date by the serial number at checkcoverage.apple.com
manualCarrierLock: Settings > General > About > Carrier Lock: it should say “No SIM restrictions”
manualFunctions: Whether {bio}, True Tone, the cameras, speakers, microphones, buttons and vibration work
manualExterior: Exterior: frame, screen scratches, screws, gaps and liquid indicators
partsNote: The serial numbers the parts report now. Their factory record cannot be read over the cable, so they do not tell whether a part was replaced; compare them with a repair record or the parts' labels
stepDiagnostics: Reading the battery and hardware diagnostics
stepAnalytics: Reading battery records from the analytics logs
errorNoUsbmuxd: Cannot reach usbmuxd: install iTunes or Apple Devices (Windows), or start usbmuxd (Linux)
errorPairingPending: Tap “Trust” on the iPhone and enter its passcode
errorPasswordLocked: Unlock the iPhone's screen first to pair it
errorUserDenied: “Don't Trust” was chosen on the iPhone
errorNoDevice: No device found; connect an iPhone with a cable
sidebarNoDeviceHint: Connect an iPhone with a cable and it shows up here
sidebarPrivacy: Everything runs on this computer; nothing is uploaded
pairingHint: Unlock the iPhone and choose “Trust” when it asks “Trust This Computer?”
emptySubtitle: Shows the information the device reports once it is connected; Inspect checks its hardware, system and security item by item
emptyStepConnect: Connect it to the computer with a cable
emptyStepDone: Review its information, then inspect it
attentionCount: {count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}; details in the categories below
manualHint: Software cannot judge these reliably; check them on the phone
errorsTitle: Items that could not be read
batteryFootnote: Live values come from the battery's gas gauge (IORegistry AppleSmartBattery); the “analytics log” values from the analytics iOS records daily, which Settings > Battery Health uses. Whether the battery is genuine, check in Settings > Battery and in Parts and Service History.
rawIntro: The data exactly as the device returned it, unprocessed, to verify the verdicts against.
cliReport: print the inspection report in the terminal
cliJSON: print the inspection report as JSON, with every raw value
cliDump: query the IORegistry item by item and write the replies to this file (with a summary in .txt), to find parts' information
cliLang: the report's language: en, zh-Hans or de (default: the system's)
cliPairing: The device does not trust this computer yet; asking to pair…
cliProbing: Querying the IORegistry ({count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}})…
overviewHint: Inspecting also reads the diagnostics, battery logs, apps and profiles, and gives a verdict on each item
storageUsage: {used, number, ::.0} GB used of {total, number, ::.0} GB
